question: At fixed D11 training batches and frozen snapshots, how large and compatible are the existing SK and relative-XY auxiliary parameter gradients?
diagnostic_objective: Lone+0.1*Lroll+0.2*(Lrelative_teacher+0.1*Lrelative_free), same for every snapshot including C0/common; hypothetical total at C0, not historical-update replay

snapshots.trained_objective: P3 one-step-trained common origin; diagnostic SK and auxiliary objectives are prospective

batch_selection_rules.historical_update1: Exact historical update1 slot order; exposure anchor, not population-representative inference
batch_selection_rules.D11_zero5: Every new train family once, all five applied commands zero, actual core state10 start
batch_selection_rules.D11_transition: Each new train family having an actual transition once; earliest eligible K5 start, then slot tie-break
batch_selection_rules.D11_noncontact: Each new train family having a fully noncontact K5 once; earliest eligible start, then slot tie-break

numeric_criteria.closure_meaning: heuristic reordered-backward float32 precision guard, not effect threshold
numeric_criteria.clip_meaning: compute coefficient only, parameterwise float32 norm and flat float64 norm separately; no actual clipping

analysis.opposition: cosine < -1e-6 is a local directional descriptor, not sufficient to show base loss would rise
analysis.dominance: report continuous auxiliary/base norm ratio; ratio>1 only states norm size
analysis.combined_projection: dot(g_base,g_independent_total)/norm(g_base)^2; local Euclidean descent only, not Adam
analysis.parameter_blocks: all six tensors, fixed parameter order
limits: Snapshots differ in weights and training histories; comparisons do not identify whole-training causality
Probe windows/families/transitions overlap, not independent experiments
Transition and noncontact probes have different geometry, not matched causal controls
No claim of optimal beta, data sufficiency, overfitting, independent generalization or alignment improvement
